newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH EMU DECISION AS LATE AS POSSIBLE - TUOMIOJA.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH EMU DECISION AS LATE AS POSSIBLE - TUOMIOJA.

text.p: Parliament should decide as late as possible whether Finland should join Europe's single currency, Social Democratic Party (SDP) parliamentary group leader Erkki Tuomioja said in a book published on Monday.

"It is not wise to decide on Finland's stance before it is necessary. This means that parliament should determine its stance only just before the decisive meeting of the European council," Tuomioja wrote.
A summit of EU heads of state and government in spring 1998 is due to decide which countries qualify for the third stage of Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) slated for start-up in 1999.
Like most Finnish political groups, SDP, the biggest party in parliament and government, is divided over EMU. Tuomioja said he had not made up his own mind yet.

"The intention of this book is to help clarify which kind of and how important issues are at stake. My intention is not to dictate what one should think about them because I cannot yet say what my own final stance will be," he wrote.
He called for broad and critical debate on EMU.
"The finance ministry's EMU reports ... don't enjoy nor do they deserve such confidence that they would be a sufficient base for the decision," Tuomioja said.
The finance ministry said in a report on October 3 that the prospects for economic growth and a favourable employment trend would be better for Finland inside EMU than outside.

"Economic and Monetary Union will not solve Finland's main topical problems. It will, however, provide better conditions for favourable growth and employment trends than remaining outside the Euro-area," the ministry said.
"EMU will enhance the pre-requisites for an economic policy that supports growth and employment," the report said.
Tuomioja said the ministry was too obviously pro-EMU and called for unbiased studies on the single currency.

A report by an expert group lead by economics professor Jukka Pekkarinen would provide "a valuable addition" to base a decision on although the group's mandate does not include making a recommendation for or against Finnish EMU membership, he said.
The Pekkarinen report is due this spring.
Tuomioja said Sweden's EMU decision could affect Finland's.

"If Sweden remains outside EMU at least in the beginning it will make it more justifiable and easier for Finland to remain outside and the opposite, a Swedish decision to participate in EMU would add pressures on Finland to join monetary union at the same time," he wrote.
